title: Quant exception litmus run for FinSolve low-latency trading model
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Support ticket from customer FinSolve requesting an exception to allow FP8 quantization for their low-latency trading ranking model (llama-2-13b-custom) despite our default policy that prefers INT8 for this model family. Customer reports cost and latency constraints and requests a bespoke calibration run with their anonymized seed set and a short litmus evaluation to validate that accuracy stays within a 1.5% regression window on risk-sensitive signals. This ticket tracks engineering work to run the calibration, evaluate accuracy regressions on customer-provided and internal holdout sets, and produce a recommended quant-profile or a safe rollback policy. Deliverables: calibration artifacts, accuracy report, suggested quant-profile override YAML, support playbook for approval and follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Run FP8 calibration with customer seed set and internal replication. 2) Produce per-signal metric table showing deltas vs baseline (float16) and vs INT8 baseline. 3) If regression <= 1.5% on critical signals, produce quant-profile and rollback config for Dedicated/Private. 4) Document reproducible steps, PRs, and approval notes for Customer Success to close support case.
comments: 2025-09-03 - Aisha Raman: Initial triage with Support. Customer provided three anonymized datasets (market_signals_1.csv, trade_labels_2.csv, drift_samples.json) and a baseline float16 run. Customer explicitly requests FP8 because INT8 path increases tail latency in their infra stack due to additional kernel conversions.

2025-09-04 - Mateo Alvarez: Reproduced baseline float16 on our infra; initial INT8 auto-calib run completed. Noted that INT8 reduced model size but introduced a 2.7% regression on the 'liquidity_spike' metric vs float16. Logging a hypothesis that scoring-sensitive heads lose dynamic range under current INT8 calibration settings.

2025-09-06 - Mateo Alvarez: Started FP8 calibration with two quant-profile seeds (qprof-A: per-channel symmetric, qprof-B: asymmetric per-tensor). Ran on a dedicated GPU pool to avoid co-tenancy noise. Initial FP8 qprof-A shows 0.9% regression on 'liquidity_spike' and negligible impact on ranking NDCG@10.

2025-09-08 - Data Science (Rong He): Performed statistical significance tests. The 0.9% regression for qprof-A is within target but shows higher variance on tail samples. Recommended an additional KV-cache stability run with longer prefix lengths to ensure no cache-induced drift.

2025-09-10 - Mateo Alvarez: Ran KV-cache stability test and observed drift in one embed-dense head for sequences >512 tokens. Mitigation: apply bias-correction fold and tighten calibration histogram buckets for that layer. Re-ran; delta reduced to 0.6%.

2025-09-12 - Customer Success (Lena Park): Presented interim results to FinSolve. Customer agreed to a short canary in their staging account if engineering produces clear rollback instructions and an automatic fallback to INT8 if error rate or latency exceed thresholds.

2025-09-15 - Mateo Alvarez: Drafted quant-profile override (qprof-finSolve-v1.yaml) and rollout plan with canary route: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with auto-fallback to INT8 runtime variant and telemetry checks for NDCG, latency p95, and error rate. Filed PR: calib-harness#289. Marking ticket In Progress for final validation and approval.
Notes: Links to PR and Confluence contain raw calibration logs, numeric histograms, and the small script used to apply bias-correction.
technical_notes:
- Model: llama-2-13b-custom (tokenizer v14).
- Baseline: float16 running on a8x GPUs.
- Calibration harness: calib-harness v0.9.2 with histogram-clip=1e-4 and per-channel stats.
- Candidate profiles: qprof-A (FP8 symmetric per-channel), qprof-B (FP8 asymmetric per-tensor), control INT8 profile from release runtime-1.24.
- Evaluation metrics: NDCG@10 (primary), liquidity_spike_recall (custom binary), latency p95.
- Risk: FP8 introduces higher variance in rare tail signals; mitigation requires bias-correction and a staged canary with automatic fallback.
next_steps: 1) Final validation run on a larger holdout (10k examples) by 2025-09-18. 2) Merge PR and create release note for support playbook. 3) Coordinate with Customer Success to initiate staged canary with FinSolve. 4) If any metric exceeds thresholds during canary, trigger immediate rollback and open postmortem.
postmortem_plan: If canary fails, capture end-to-end traces, token-level delta samples, and reproduce failure on our isolated infra. Create a short postmortem with timeline, root cause, and proposed mitigation (expected within 3 working days).
qa_checks:
- Reproducibility: run seed=42 across 3 different GPU types.
- Determinism: ensure kernel selections logged and compare token outputs for 100 sample prompts.
- Telemetry: create dashboard for NDCG, latency p95, error rate with alert thresholds per rollout step.
owner_notes: Mateo: prefer to finalize a qprof-A derivative (qprof-finSolve-v1) that includes the per-layer bias-correction patch. Will push a small tuning script to calib-harness and request a quick security review before customer rollout.
resolution_criteria: Ticket can be closed when customer confirms canary completion within agreed thresholds, the quant-profile is stored in the catalog with an exception flag, and all artifacts (logs, PRs, playbook) are linked in Confluence.
